extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / differential geometry (working on Ricci flow and 3-manifold topology)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the technical assumptions, neighborhood classifications, curvature/volume estimates, and surgical construction requirements used to define and run Ricci flow with surgery on three-dimensional, compact orientable manifolds (Perelman-style). Useful for verifying that a solution or surgery procedure satisfies the hypotheses used in theorems and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative estimates near high curvature points (7.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ε>0 and a solution (M,gij(·,t)) there is r0>0 such that each point (x,t) with R(x,t) ≥ r0^{-2} satisfies the derivative estimates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: |∇R|(x,t) < η R^{3/2}(x,t) and |∂R/∂t|(x,t) < η R^2(x,t), where η>0 is a universal constant. Moreover such points have a canonical neighborhood which is either an evolving ε-neck, an evolving ε-cap, or a compact positively curved manifold (in which case the solution becomes extinct). (This gives control of gradients/time-derivatives in high curvature regions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman volume–curvature estimate (Theorem 7.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any w>0 there exist τ(w)>0, K(w)<∞, α(w)>0 such that: if a three-dimensional, compact orientable normalized solution on [0,T) and for some r0<α and (x0,t0) the solution on the ball Bt0(x0,r0) satisfies appropriate lower curvature bound at time t0 and Vol_{t0}(Bt0(x0,r0)) ≥ w r0^3,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: then R(x,t) ≤ 2 K r0^{-2} whenever t ∈ [t0−τ r0^2, t0] and d_t(x,x0) ≤ r0. (In words: a lower curvature bound at a time slice together with a volume lower bound controls the scalar curvature backwards in time on a parabolic neighborhood.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: uniform curvature control with radius-volume parameters (Corollary 7.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any w>0 and A<∞ there exist τ(w,A), K(w,A), α(w,A)>0 such that under the same hypotheses as Theorem 7.2.2 with an additional distance parameter A, one gets uniform curvature bounds R(x,t) ≤ K r0^{-2} on the stated parabolic/distance region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the scaled/parameterized version used when one needs control on regions whose distances from the base point are bounded by A·r0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman local collapsing/volume consequence (Corollary 7.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any w>0 there exists ρ(w)>0 such that if gij(t) is a complete normalized solution on M (three-dimensional, compact, orientable) and Bt0(x0,r0) at time t0≥1 has r0<ρ and min_{x∈Bt0(x0,r0)} Rm(x,t0) = − r0^{-2},
rubrics_metrics.guidance: then Vol_{t0}(Bt0(x0,r0)) ≤ w r0^3. (I.e. if the minimum sectional curvature reaches −r0^{-2} on a sufficiently small scale then the ball must have correspondingly small volume.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Ricci flow with surgery (Definition 7.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Ricci flow with surgery is a (finite or countably infinite) collection of smooth three-dimensional Ricci flow solutions g_kij(t) on compact orientable manifolds M_k defined on time intervals [t_k^-, t_k^+), together with their limits (Ω_k, ar g_kij) as t -> t_k^+ and the property that certain compact submanifolds (possibly disconnected) in these limit metrics are isometric between successive pieces; by identifying these isometric submanifolds one obtains a surgically modified solution on the union of the time intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The times t_k^+ are called surgery times. This definition formalizes cutting and gluing operations at singular times by matching isometric limit pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: A priori assumptions for surgically modified solutions — Pinching assumption (7.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The eigenvalues λ ≥ μ ≥ ν of the curvature operator of the solution (at every point and time) satisfy a pinching inequality (displayed as (7.3.3)) whenever ν<0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text presents the explicit pinching inequality (7.3.3) (Perelman-style logarithmic pinching) and requires it hold at every point/time for surgically modified solutions with the stated accuracy. This controls negative eigenvalues and provides the curvature pinching needed in the canonical neighborhood analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: A priori assumptions for surgically modified solutions — Canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any ε>0 there exist positive constants C1,C2 (depending only on ε) and a positive nonincreasing function r(t) so that at each time t>0 every point x with scalar curvature R(x,t) ≥ r(t)^{-2} has a neighborhood B = B_t(x,σ) (with B_t(x,2σ) ⊂ …) falling into one of three categories:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) B is a strong ε-neck (slice of a parabolic neighborhood ε-close to the evolving standard round cylinder after scaling by R(x,t)); (b) B is an ε-cap; (c) B is a compact manifold (without boundary) of positive sectional curvature. Furthermore the scalar curvature in B at time t is between C2^{-1} R(x,t) and C2 R(x,t), the gradient estimates |∂R/∂t|<η R^2 and |∇R|<η R^{3/2} hold in B (equation (7.3.4)), and the volume of B in cases (a) and (b) satisfies (C2 R(x,t))^{-3/2} Vol_t(B) ≤ ε σ^3. (These provide both geometric shape and quantitative size/control of canonical neighborhoods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of ε-neck/ε-cap containing subsets (types (a)–(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the limit metric (Ω,�bar g) every ε-neck is contained in a subset of one of the following types: (a) an ε-tube with boundary components in Ω_ρ; (b) an ε-cap with boundary in Ω_ρ; (c) an ε-horn with boundary in Ω_ρ; (d) a capped ε-horn; (e) a double ε-horn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: ε-tube/ε-horn/double-ε-horn/capped-ε-horn depend on whether scalar curvature stays bounded or tends to infinity on ends; this classification is used to locate where to perform cuts (surgery) and how to compactify horns by gluing caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery selection guideline — only cut ε-horns at sufficiently fine necks
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing surgery one should cut ε-horns (not arbitrary ε-tubes or ε-caps) and cut them at 'fine' necks and glue 'fine' caps; δ will be chosen much smaller than ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: one cannot, in general, find fine necks in an ε-tube or ε-cap; performing surgeries at rough necks loses accuracy and errors could accumulate over repeated surgeries so as to destroy recognizability of high-curvature regions. Hence surgeries are restricted to ε-horns at fine scales to control errors and ensure finiteness of surgeries in finite time intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of fine δ-necks inside ε-horns (Lemma 7.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0<ε<1/100, 0<δ<ε and 0<T<∞ there exists 0<h<δ ρ (depending only on δ and r(T)) such that: if a solution to Ricci flow with surgery satisfies the a priori assumptions and (Ω,�bar g) is the limit at time T, then for each point x in an ε-horn of (Ω,�bar g) with boundary in Ω_ρ and with h(x)=�bar R(x)^{-1/2}, the neighborhood B_T(x,δ^{-1} h(x)) is a strong δ-neck (i.e., after scaling by h(x)^{-2} and shifting time it is δ-close in C^{[δ^{-1}]} to the standard evolving round cylinder on the parabolic interval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucially, h depends only on δ and r(T) and is independent of the particular surgical solution; this uniformity guarantees one can cut off enough volume at each surgery and keep the number of surgeries finite on finite time intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curvature estimate for standard capped infinite-cylinder solutions (Proposition 7.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If gij is a complete Riemannian metric on R^n (n≥3) with nonnegative curvature operator and positive scalar curvature asymptotic to a round cylinder at infinity (a 'standard capped infinite cylinder'), then the Ricci flow with this initial data exists on a maximal time interval [0,T) (with T>0) and the solution has bounded curvature on each compact time subinterval and satisfies a lower bound on scalar curvature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically there exists C (depending only on the initial metric) such that R(x,t) ≥ C^{-1}/(T - t) (the text gives an explicit estimate of the form R(x,t) ≥ C^{-1}( ... ) depending on n and T). This provides the model curvature blow-up behavior used for glued caps (the 'standard solution' used to cap horns).
